choices.misconception: I took 3 away from the tens digit instead of from the whole number.
I counted back one step too many.
I counted 51, 50, 49 and counted 51 as one of the three steps.
I added 3 instead of taking 3 away.

hints: Count back one step at a time.
Picture 51 on a number line and take three steps to the left. Only the steps count, not the number you start on. Be careful as you go back past 50.
One step back from 51 is 50, two steps back is 49. Take one more step.

solutions.reliable: Start at 51 and step back three times: 50, 49, 48. So 3 less than 51 is 48. Check: 48 + 3 = 51. The idea to keep: on a number line count the jumps, not the number you start on.
solutions.elegant: Take 1 to reach 50, then 2 more to reach 48. The idea to keep: break a jump at a round number.

whyOnTest: Counting back across a ten is where off-by-one slips happen, and the number line keeps the steps honest.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
